zimbabwe-food-riots-1998.whole: The 1991-95 adjustment programme aimed for 5% yearly growth, inflation down from 17.7% to 10% and a budget deficit cut from over 10% to 5% of GDP (the government's own targets, as quoted by SEATINI from a 1999 UNDP report). The World Bank's own evaluation office found real GDP grew about 4.7% a year in 1994-97, but inflation stayed at 21%, deficits averaged 8.8% of GDP in 1993/94-1997/98, and growth fell to 2.5% in 1998 and below zero after. It rated the second adjustment credit's outcome 'highly unsatisfactory' and said it 'did not achieve its objectives'. Brett and Winter (Helen Suzman Foundation) point also to the 1992 and 1995 droughts.

chevron-ks-endeavor-koluama.whole: After the January 2012 fire, Chevron Nigeria sealed and abandoned the Funiwa 1A natural gas well, using a relief well drilled by Transocean's GSF Baltic rig (Oil & Gas Journal, June 2012). No figures were found for gas the well produced or was meant to supply.

socfin-malen-2019.whole: By Socfin's own count, 18,443 hectares were identified for its Sierra Leone project and 12,349 hectares of oil palm were planted; the company produced 50,249 tonnes of palm oil (year not stated) and had 5,865 direct and indirect workers at end-2023. It does not disclose land rent paid. No independent check was found.

barrick-pierina-jangas-killings.whole: Pierina opened in 1998 as the first mine Barrick built and ran in South America. After about 15 years, mining in the pit ended in August 2013 and closure began under the mine's closure plan (Barrick). No figures on gold output, taxes or jobs were found. This is the company's own account; no independent check was found.

chiatura-georgian-manganese.whole: The Chiatura mines produced 400,000 tonnes of manganese concentrate in 2019, down from an estimated 580,000 tonnes in 2018 because of a strike (US Geological Survey). Ferroalloys, including those from the company's Zestafoni plant, made up 8.0% of Georgia's export value in 2019.

cochabamba-water-war.whole: Aguas del Tunari ran the system from 1 November 1999 until the contract was ended in April 2000. Bechtel says it raised water availability by 30% in that time, and that about half of the 35% average rate rise paid government requirements, including over $30 million of the old utility's debt; no independent check of these claims was found. Bechtel and Abengoa later dropped a $50 million claim for a token payment in January 2006 (CorpWatch).

embobut-sengwer.whole: The US$68.5 million IDA credit aimed to improve water and forest management in selected districts. By the World Bank's 2011 restructuring paper, 141,000 hectares of forest were under approved plans and 1,790 hectares of new forest cover planted, against 2013 targets of 300,000 and 3,500 hectares; the project was rated 'moderately satisfactory' in 2011. The Inspection Panel later found it did not apply the Bank's safeguards for indigenous peoples (Bretton Woods Project). The progress figures are the World Bank's own; no independent check of them was found.

chico-river-dam.whole: The dams were never built. After the murder of Macli-ing Dulag in April 1980, the World Bank withdrew from the project and the martial-law government cancelled its plans (Bantayog ng mga Bayani).

rcbc-coal-plants.whole: IFC said it invested in RCBC from 2011 to 'strengthen the financial sector in the Philippines' after the global financial crisis, with aims including financial inclusion. RCBC financed 10 coal power plants and committed to finance an 11th. After the CAO investigation, IFC's board approved an action plan in 2022 to assess the plants' impacts and emissions (IFC). IFC gave no figures on what its investment achieved; no independent check was found.

nsel-chichigalpa-ckd.whole: No figures were found on the sugar, ethanol, power or jobs the IFC-backed expansion produced. Through the CAO dialogue, about US$2.7 million (about $1 million at first, then nearly $1.7 million from sugar-industry associations) funded Boston University research, which found the kidney disease's cause unknown but likely linked to work, with heat stress a likely factor. The CAO, the IFC's complaints office, reports monthly food aid to over 2,500 families (over $4 million in total) and 100 houses built by NSEL with the Inter-American Development Bank and others (CAO, 2015). No independent check was found.

cote-divoire-1990-pay-cuts.whole: In 1990 Côte d'Ivoire owed $14.2 billion abroad, among the highest per head in the world, and cocoa prices had fallen by more than half since 1987 (Christian Science Monitor). The government said the pay cuts had to save $456 million to unlock about $4.4 billion of aid from creditors over two years. No figures on what the programme later achieved were found.

paraguay-2002-privatization-protests.whole: When the IMF pressed for the telecoms and water privatisations, Paraguay's economy shrank 0.4% in 2000 (3.0% per person), inflation was about 9% and the public deficit was 5.7% of GDP, by the IMF's figures. The IMF said poverty had 'deepened - especially in rural areas' and warned against using sale proceeds to cover spending overruns. No figures on the programme's later results were found. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

togo-june-2010-fuel.whole: The IMF's three-year credit arrangement for Togo was worth about US$140.8 million, of which US$106.7 million had been paid out by mid-2010. By the IMF's count, growth was expected at about 3.4% in 2010, average inflation was 2.1% at end-June 2010 and the budget deficit was expected at about 2.9% of GDP, and Togo was on track to reach the HIPC debt-relief completion point in December 2010. These are IMF figures; no independent check was found.

arequipazo-2002.whole: Peru's IMF programme assumed US$870 million from privatisations by end-2002; the government expected only about US$400 million, and the sale of two state companies set for mid-2002 was delayed (IMF letter of intent, November 2002). The same letter put 2002 growth at 3.7%, inflation at about 2% and the deficit at 2.3% of GDP. These are government and IMF figures; no independent check was found.

cutral-co-ypf.whole: The government sold 46% of YPF in July 1993 and 22% more in September 1993, putting most of the company in private hands; a restructuring study cut staff from 40,000 to 10,000 (World Bank completion report). The Bank rated its related US$28 million engineering loan 'satisfactory', though only US$8.3 million was used before it was prepaid in 1994. No sale proceeds were given. These are World Bank figures; no independent check was found.

koh-kong-sugar-evictions.whole: Two KSL-run companies received 19,100 hectares in Koh Kong in August 2006 and in 2009 won a contract to supply sugar to Tate & Lyle (CorpWatch). Tate & Lyle's US parent, ASR, held an exclusive contract to buy all the plantation's sugar (OECD Watch). No figures on output, exports or jobs were found.

mallku-khota-south-american-silver.whole: The silver-indium-gallium project was never mined by the company. After Bolivia revoked the licence, an arbitration tribunal in 2018 awarded South American Silver US$18.7 million in amounts invested plus about US$9 million interest, against its US$307.2 million valuation. Bolivia's government says the state now owns the deposit, which it values at US$8 billion (company release, November 2018). No independent account of the award was opened.

tonkolili-bumbuna-police.whole: African Minerals built the mine, refurbishing 31 miles and building 51 miles of railway to carry iron ore to the coast; it employed about 7,000 people in 2012 and was described by the UK Court of Appeal as 'a flagship project for Sierra Leone'. Human Rights Watch described the mining company as the country's largest private employer, and said the economy grew 21% in 2012 (citing the IMF). The mine has since closed.

smurfit-kappa-cajibio-misak.whole: Smurfit Kappa's Colombian arm has 70,000 hectares of plantations across six departments, about a third of them in Cauca, including 3,000 hectares at Cajibío, and manages about 22,000 hectares of natural forest (Mongabay, 2022). By the company's own reports, it generated 2,613 jobs in Colombia in 2018 and made about $29 million profit there in 2021. Its Cauca paper products carry an FSC label audited by a third party (Mongabay).
